title: Research and Publications
text:
Peer-reviewed publications




Factor timing with transaction costs


Vaibhav Lalwani and Ashok Gunturu


Borsa Istanbul Review · 100913 · 2026


DOI



Times factor exposures using 50 net-of-cost smart-beta factors, driven by their past returns and covariances. The dynamic strategy beats a static 1/N benchmark on risk-adjusted returns even after 2000's fading premiums, with low turnover and results robust to specification choices.





Climate news betas and risk premia


Vaibhav Lalwani


Energy Economics · 157, 109289 · 2026


DOI



Tests whether climate-news betas are priced in US and Chinese stocks, and shows the answer swings widely with innocuous modelling choices. After correcting for multiple testing, no climate-risk premium survives.





Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning: The Role of Research Design Choices


Vaibhav Lalwani, Vedprakash Vasantrao Meshram and Varun Jindal


European Financial Management · 32(3), 816–833 · 2025


DOIPDF



Shows that research-design choices move machine-learning portfolio returns so much that their nonstandard errors are up to five times the usual standard errors. Even so, ML still earns net-of-cost returns for about a third of portfolios.





Does economic complexity tame the stock markets? International evidence


Vaibhav Lalwani and Kirti Saxena


Applied Economics · 1–17 · 2025


DOI



Shows that countries producing more diverse and unique goods tend to have calmer stock markets. The effect is concentrated in emerging markets and only kicks in past a complexity threshold.





Finfluencer recommendations


Vaibhav Lalwani


Economics Letters · 255, 112511 · 2025


DOI



Studies stock calls from Indian financial YouTubers. Finfluencers favour past winners with heavy trading, rich valuations, and high intraday activity, and the number of their recommendations predicts future returns.





Mean-variance optimization and the cross-section of stock returns


Vaibhav Lalwani


Global Finance Journal · 66, 101130 · 2025


DOI



Builds an asset-pricing factor from Sharpe-ratio-maximising mean-variance weights, and finds it is priced in the cross-section of stocks and bonds, out of sample and across countries.





Forecasting equity returns with oil prices: addressing model choice uncertainty


Vaibhav Lalwani and Udayan Sharma


Applied Economics · 57(5), 566–582 · 2024


DOI



Adapts extreme bounds analysis to out-of-sample forecasting, and finds oil prices carry incremental information for aggregate and sectoral stock returns once combined with other oil variables.





Inflation hedging via tracking portfolios in the BRICS markets


Vedprakash Vasantrao Meshram and Vaibhav Lalwani


Cogent Economics & Finance · 12(1) · 2024


DOI



Builds portfolios that track unexpected CPI inflation in the BRICS markets. Statistical tracking beats the benchmarks, especially when inflation uncertainty is low.





Climate risks, corporate bonds, and economic uncertainty


Vaibhav Lalwani


Economics Letters · 244, 111984 · 2024


DOI



Shows corporate bonds that move with global-warming news earn lower returns. The gap shows up mainly in periods of high economic policy uncertainty, when investors pay up for climate-resilient bonds.





Incorporating green assets in equity portfolios


Vaibhav Lalwani


Finance research letters · 59, 104815 · 2023


DOI



Adds green-asset ETFs to mean-variance portfolios. Mixing them with broad market indices lifts returns and Sharpe ratios, survives transaction costs, and long-horizon investors are more likely to beat the benchmark.





ARE FACTOR INVESTING STRATEGIES SUCCESSFUL OUT-OF-SAMPLE: EVIDENCE FROM THE NIFTY INDICES


Vaibhav Lalwani


Applied Finance Letters · 11, 94–108 · 2023


DOILink



Shows that most NSE factor indices stop earning their past returns once they go live, and none deliver alpha over size, value, and momentum.





The cross-section of Indian stock returns: evidence using machine learning


Vaibhav Lalwani and Vedprakash Vasantrao Meshram


Applied Economics · 54(16), 1814–1828 · 2021


DOI



Tests 35 characteristics on every listed Indian firm and finds machine learning forecasts beat OLS, with the best portfolios earning significant returns.





Predicting Intraday cryptocurrency returns – A Sparse Signals approach


Vaibhav Lalwani and Vedprakash Vasantrao Meshram


The Journal of Prediction Markets · 15(1) · 2021


DOI



Finds sparse, short-lived signals in minute-by-minute cryptocurrency returns, with LASSO forecasts beating the usual benchmarks.





Stock Market Efficiency in the Time of COVID-19: Evidence from Industry Stock Returns


Vaibhav Lalwani and Vedprakash Vasantrao Meshram


International Journal of Accounting & Finance Review · 5(2), 40–44 · 2020


DOIPDF



Shows stock-return predictability rose in several industries after COVID-19 hit, suggesting markets became less informationally efficient.





Multi-factor asset pricing models in emerging and developed markets


Vaibhav Lalwani and Madhumita Chakraborty


Managerial Finance · 46(3), 360–380 · 2019


DOI



Compares multi-factor models across ten markets. The Fama-French five-factor model prices stocks best in Australia, Canada, China, and the US, but not everywhere.





Aggregate earnings and gross domestic product: International evidence


Vaibhav Lalwani and Madhumita Chakraborty


Applied Economics · 52(1), 68–84 · 2019


DOI



Shows the link between aggregate earnings and real GDP growth holds across eight countries, and that forecasters underreact to aggregate earnings news.





Investor reaction to extreme price shocks in stock markets: A cross country examination


Vaibhav Lalwani, Udayan Sharma and Madhumita Chakraborty


IIMB Management Review · 31(3), 258–267 · 2019


DOIPDF



Documents over- and under-reaction after extreme intraday moves in the ten largest markets, pointing to exploitable behavioural biases.





Asset pricing factors and future economic growth


Vaibhav Lalwani and Madhumita Chakraborty


Economics Letters · 168, 151–154 · 2018


DOI



Tests seven common asset-pricing factors against future GDP and industrial-production growth, and finds only the market factor predicts it. The predictive power reported in earlier studies looks to have faded.





Quality investing in the Indian stock market


Vaibhav Lalwani and Madhumita Chakraborty


Managerial Finance · 44(2), 127–141 · 2018


DOI



Finds two of four quality screens beat the market on BSE-500 stocks, even after controlling for size, value, and momentum.

title: Research and Publications
text:
Working papers & preprints




YouTubers and Stock Returns


Vaibhav Lalwani and Vedprakash Vasantrao Meshram


SSRN Electronic Journal · 2026


DOI



Uses a large language model to pull stock calls from YouTubers across nine countries. The calls predict one-month returns, but not longer-horizon moves or lasting profits.





The Value Relevance of Earnings for Factor Investors


Vaibhav Lalwani and Madhumita Chakraborty


SSRN Electronic Journal · 2024


DOI



Shows the aggregate earnings-returns link is stronger for large-cap and growth stocks than for small-cap and value stocks, with implications for factor investors.

title: Vaibhav Lalwani
text:
Associate Professor, Finance


XLRI — Xavier School of Management · Delhi-NCR, India


Google Scholar · LinkedIn · vaibhav@xlri.ac.in
I am an Associate Professor in Finance at the Xavier Labour Relations Institute’s (XLRI) Delhi-NCR Campus. My research interests include asset pricing, AI/ML in investment strategies, and climate risk.
I received the Prof. M. J. Manohar Rao Young Economist Award for the Year 2024, awarded by The Indian Econometric Society (TIES).

title: Data and Code
text: I am an avid R programmer. In this section I share code and material that I have found useful for my research, along with links to other helpful websites containing code and data.

title: Data and Code
text:
My Datasets and Code

International Asset Pricing Factor Dataset — asset pricing factor portfolios for ten countries from 1993 to 2017 (built from Datastream data). The factors are created using book-to-market, price-to-earnings, investment, momentum, profitability, and quality characteristics. Refer to this paper for more information. These factors are no longer updated.

title: Data and Code
text:
Free Data Sources for Research

Asset Pricing and Factors


Ken French Data Library — the classic US and international factor portfolios, industry returns, and portfolio sorts.


AQR Data Sets — factor, style, and strategy return series (value, momentum, quality, betting-against-beta, and more).


Robert Shiller’s Online Data — long-run stock market series, CAPE, earnings, and US home prices.




Firm Fundamentals and Financial Data


Aswath Damodaran’s Data — cost of capital, betas, country risk premiums, and industry-level financial data.


SEC EDGAR — company filings (10-K, 10-Q, and more); bulk financials in the Financial Statement Data Sets.


Nasdaq Data Link — a large catalogue of free macroeconomic and financial time series.

Websites and Other Useful Material
Useful material for academics in Economics, Finance, and/or Accounting.

Readings / Websites


Econ Journal Watch — a nice collection of articles with critical takes on topics of academic interest.


Critical Finance Review — critical papers on finance; a must-read for Finance/Accounting academics.


Andrew Gelman’s Blog — causality, Bayesian statistics, and statistical pitfalls in pop-science research.




Datasets and Code


JKP Factors — asset pricing factor data for many countries from Compustat Global.


Open Source Asset Pricing — data on asset pricing factors plus code for generating factors from CRSP/Compustat.




Data Science and Programming


Tidy Finance — the best way to learn R programming for financial analysis and research.
